newsitem.title: INDONESIA: East Timorese students stage protest in Dili.
newsitem.headline: East Timorese students stage protest in Dili.

text.p: More than 1,000 East Timorese students demonstrated outside Dili's university on Wednesday against Indonesian criticism of the territory's Nobel Peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo, an official in Dili said.
"They are reacting strongly to statements and demonstrations against the bishop in Jakarta," Armindo Maia, vice-rector of the University of East Timor, told Reuters by telephone from Dili.

He said there had been no confrontation so far between the students and security forces, who have kept a tight clamp on the territory in the run-up to Tuesday's fifth anniversary of the killing of at least 50 protesters.

"It's a bit tense. We are trying to overcome the situation. The students are gathering here at the university, not only university students but senior high school students in front of the university," Maia said.
More than 2,000 members of youth groups allied to Indonesia's ruling Golkar Party demonstrated outside parliament in Jakarta on Tuesday demanding Belo be expelled from the country.
Belo has come under attack for reportedly saying in an interview with the German news magazine Der Spiegel that Indonesian troops had trampled on East Timor's independence "and treated us like dogs".

The bishop, one of the most respected men in strongly Catholic East Timor, has declined to comment until he sees a full text of the interview. He was in Jakarta for an annual meeting of Catholic bishops.

Students in Dili also held a peaceful demonstration at the university on Tuesday after a heated discussion with representatives of Indonesia's official National Commission on Human Rights on campus a day earlier.

Indonesian troops invaded the former Portuguese colony in December 1975 and Jakarta incorporated the territory as its 27th province the following July in a move the United Nations has refused to recognise.
